newsitem.title: PERU: Peru ends dangerous search for mudslide victims.
newsitem.headline: Peru ends dangerous search for mudslide victims.

text.p: The bodies of up to 300 peasants will remain entombed under a thick crust of mud in southeastern Peru after authorities decided on Saturday the risk to rescuers from mudslides or epidemics was too great to continue digging.
"It is better to save our own lives than recover dead people," Luis Barra, mayor of the village of Abancay and local civil defence chief, told Reuters by telephone.

Rescuers on Saturday dug another four bodies out of the mud and rocks which engulfed the Andean mountain villages of Ccocha and Pumaranra before dawn on Tuesday. But driving rain triggered a fresh mudslide and they abandoned their work.
"We worked from eight in the morning (1300 GMT) to two (1900 GMt) in the afternoon, when more mud came sliding down, which scared us. So we decided to call off the search," Barra said.
Nearly 50 bodies have been recovered by civil defence workers who have laboured under the constant threat of the mudslides that are common in Peru's rainy season.

Barra said bodies closest to the surface have now been found, but the rest were more than two yards (meters) below. The buried bodies were beginning to rot, and posed less of a threat of causing epidemics if they were left under mud.
Their advanced state of putrefaction made the bodies found on Saturday -- the legless corpse of a woman, a girl and two children -- impossible to identify.
With the rain still pouring down, exposed nearby villages have been evacuated by troops who went from hut to hut to persuade reluctant residents to leave behind their chickens, sheep and guinea pigs.
About 250 familes have lost their homes, and another 230 have been evacuated from exposed sites, Barra said. Many acres of crops have also been covered by the mud.
Survivors are spending their nights in makeshift tents and government shelters. Many told harrowing tales of narrow escapes and the deaths of their relatives.

Accompanied by an Andean brass band, mourners filed from a mass through Tamburco bearing their dead in coffins. Barra said the remaining bodies would be placed underground without ceremony due to the danger of disease.
Wet season downpours in northern Peru have also caused floods and mudslides in the Amazon region, leaving hundreds of families homeless and many people missing.
